_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI) caused or suspected to be caused by susceptible isolates of designated Gram-positive microorganisms

pivotal_trials.design: Global, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, parallel-group non-inferiority trial comparing a single 1200 mg IV dose of oritavancin to IV vancomycin for 7 to 10 days
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with clinically documented ABSSSI suspected or proven to be due to Gram-positive pathogens
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Early clinical response (composite: cessation of spread or reduction in size of baseline lesion, absence of fever, and no rescue antibacterial drug) at 48 to 72 hours after initiation of therapy; prespecified non-inferiority margin of 10%
pivotal_trials.result: Early clinical response 82.3% (391/475) oritavancin vs 78.9% (378/479) vancomycin; difference 3.4% (95% CI -1.6, 8.4), meeting non-inferiority

pivotal_trials.design: Global, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, parallel-group non-inferiority trial comparing a single 1200 mg IV dose of oritavancin to IV vancomycin for 7 to 10 days
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with clinically documented ABSSSI suspected or proven to be due to Gram-positive pathogens
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Early clinical response (composite: cessation of spread or reduction in size of baseline lesion, absence of fever, and no rescue antibacterial drug) at 48 to 72 hours after initiation of therapy; prespecified non-inferiority margin of 10%
pivotal_trials.result: Early clinical response 80.1% (403/503) oritavancin vs 82.9% (416/502) vancomycin; difference -2.7% (95% CI -7.5, 2.0), meeting non-inferiority using the prespecified margin of 10%

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=3%): headache, nausea, vomiting, limb and subcutaneous abscesses, and diarrhea. Serious adverse reactions in 5.8% (57/976) oritavancin vs 5.9% (58/983) vancomycin; most common serious AE was cellulitis (1.1% vs 1.2%). Specific rates: nausea 9.9%, headache 7.1%, vomiting 4.6%, diarrhea 3.7%.
target_moa: Semisynthetic lipoglycopeptide antibacterial with three mechanisms: inhibition of transglycosylation (cell wall polymerization), inhibition of transpeptidation (cell wall crosslinking), and disruption of bacterial membrane integrity; exerts concentration-dependent bactericidal activity

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was convened; no safety, efficacy, or other issues requiring advisory committee input were identified

basis.text: QIDP designation under the GAIN provision of FDASIA 2012 granted the application a priority review

citations.quote: Under the provisions of the Generating Antibiotic Incentives Now provision of the Food and Drug Administration Safety and Innovation Act of 2012, oritavancin diphosphate was granted Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) designation and therefore this application was granted a priority review. QIDP designation qualifies oritavancin for an additional five years of marketing exclusivity.

summary.text: Oritavancin received QIDP designation under the GAIN provision of FDASIA 2012, which conferred priority review and five years additional marketing exclusivity. Approval was based on two Phase 3 non-inferiority trials (SOLO I and SOLO II) showing non-inferiority to vancomycin for ABSSSI; no advisory committee was convened.

citations.quote: Under the provisions of the Generating Antibiotic Incentives Now provision of the Food and Drug Administration Safety and Innovation Act of 2012, oritavancin diphosphate was granted Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) designation and therefore this application was granted a priority review. QIDP designation qualifies oritavancin for an additional five years of marketing exclusivity.
Oritavancin demonstrated non-inferiority to intravenous vancomycin for the treatment of ABSSSI in two phase 3 trials.
